## TL;DR

Round 3 fixes address the review findings around shell environment propagation, Docker command forwarding, exit-code classification, and review evidence. Remote runner invocations now export their per-run environment to the selected runner script, and the Docker path forwards the project command into the container. The project command's status remains a gate result even when its exit code overlaps RepoOS's infrastructure codes. Settings keeps its dedicated command/tool inputs without overriding other generic array fields. The required changed-path check passed on this revision.

## Work and rationale

The review found that the generated remote shell command put several NAME=value assignments before a semicolon. Such assignments only apply to that shell statement; they are not inherited by the following validate.sh process. That broke project command selection, slot/container names, cache and image settings, check profile, and browser capture context. I introduced a small environment-export helper and used it in both Tailscale and Hetzner command construction. Browser capture's own prelude now uses export as well. A shell-level regression test executes the generated command with a fake runner script and records the values it sees. It checks the command, container, slot, cache volume, image, profile, offload flag, capture metadata, and positional arguments.

The Docker custom-command branch also needed to pass the exported command across the container boundary. The validation container now receives REPOOS_VALIDATION_COMMAND explicitly with Docker's -e option. The pool dispatch test now configures a custom command and required tools across two native hosts, verifies the command and export appear in each host invocation, then exercises the third job waiting until a host frees. The fixture's healthy probe response now advertises the custom-command capability. The Docker handoff passes the command as an explicit REPOOS_VALIDATION_COMMAND assignment, including an empty value when no override is configured. The test-worker cleanup set now removes that variable plus the injected cache and artifact roots so child RepoOS checks cannot inherit runner-only context. The fallback test also uses a project command and declared toolchain, preserving coverage of local fallback when remote hosts are unavailable.

A project command may legitimately return status 3, 4, or 5. Those codes overlap RepoOS's setup/transport failure classifications, so the classifier now checks for the runner's [validate] gate exit marker before applying those infrastructure meanings. Table-driven tests cover all three overlapping statuses.

The Settings review found that generic string and array controls had been inserted twice. The duplicate branch was removed so existing general settings continue using their original placeholder behavior. The Remote validation card retains its own command and required-tools inputs, and the drawer description now describes the configured project command and declared host toolchain. I added review shots for the settings inputs and host-status drawer. The settings location test confirms the command and toolchain keys resolve to rendered Remote validation rows.

Documentation now explains how runner = native affects execution and how OS/labels and runsOn choose eligible hosts, including queueing and local fallback behavior. It also clarifies that local fallback uses the project's local check plan, not the remote-only command.

## Approaches tried

I first added direct string assertions for the generated runner command. Review correctly showed these could not catch a shell assignment whose lifetime ended at a semicolon. I replaced that as the main regression guard with an actual Bash execution and a fake runner script. I also extended the existing pool queue and fallback fixtures rather than introducing a separate artificial scheduler test, so command eligibility, dispatch, and queuing are exercised together.

The initial targeted pool run failed because its host probe mock omitted the new project-command capability marker. I updated the mock to represent a compatible runner and confirmed the queue test passed. The first full changed-path check then caught missing fixture typing and capture metadata, which were corrected. Its next run exposed that the shell test expected the pre-provenance capture JSON shape; I updated the expectation to the current serialized CaptureEntry shape and reran the full check.

## Challenges and blockers

There was no live Android/Gradle runner execution in this work session. The Tiao-shaped project command fixture and remote validation framework tests cover the command and artifact path, but they do not establish that a real Android SDK/JDK installation works on bee, thinkpad, or mini. That evidence still needs a configured project and a live eligible host. The Settings host-status shot is declared against the drawer's .rvr-hosts area; a capture depends on the managed preview having host status available.

The required REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check ran against thinkpad. One initial run correctly failed on the shell test's outdated expected JSON; after fixing it, the final run passed the remote gate, all 571 selected test files, build, UI smoke, rendered contrast audit, and remaining local changed-path guards.

## Key learnings

A generated SSH command needs to be tested as a shell program, not merely inspected as text: assignment syntax, quoting, export boundaries, and nested Docker environments all affect which command actually runs. For custom runner support, capability negotiation must be reflected by fixtures as well as real probe output; otherwise tests can fail before reaching the queue behavior they intend to test. Gate exit markers also carry semantic information that numeric exit codes alone cannot preserve when project commands are arbitrary. Runner-injected environment variables must also be treated as test-process inputs and cleared consistently, while the intended gate process receives only the values it needs.
